title: Massively parallel cantilever-free atomic force microscopy

evidence.locator: Main Results, Cantilever-free probes as a distributed optical lever; Fig. 1
evidence.fact: The distributed optical lever model links backing deformation and reflection; the model estimate is about 1 nm, not demonstrated imaging precision.

evidence.locator: Main Methods, Fabrication of cantilever-free probe arrays; Fig. 1c-e
evidence.fact: Sapphire, compliant PDMS, directly written polymer probes and evaporated reflective aluminum form the array; cylinders are used for characterization.

evidence.locator: Main Results, Cantilever-free probes as a distributed optical lever; Fig. 2
evidence.fact: A 1088-probe array is mounted, leveled against flat silicon with force feedback, and optically calibrated from out-of-contact and contact states.

evidence.locator: Main Results, Topographical image reconstruction, first paragraph
evidence.fact: Vertical contact, stationary acquisition and withdrawal precede every lateral move; force-sensor evidence of release is required.

evidence.locator: Main Results, Topographical image reconstruction; Fig. 3; Methods, Image reconstruction
evidence.fact: Probe detection, per-probe intensity mapping, stitching, relative-height correction, frame offset removal and crosstalk correction form the analysis chain.

evidence.locator: Main Results, Massively parallel imaging; Fig. 4a
evidence.fact: An inert silicon calibration specimen has an arrow feature imaged at 1 micrometer lateral sampling; independent AFM depth is reported as 110 nm.

evidence.locator: Main Results, Massively parallel imaging; Fig. 4b
evidence.fact: A 100 nm lateral-step line measurement reports 126 nm mean step and 9 nm flat-region vertical precision over greater than 0.4 mm span.

evidence.locator: Main Results, Massively parallel imaging; Fig. 4c
evidence.fact: Another calibration-target region contains lines, pits and mesas; the reported acquisition is 256 seconds and processing 54 seconds.
TERA-Fab E-series, downward probes, piezo-controlled vertical/tilt and sample lateral stages, Grasshopper camera and 10x Mitutoyo NA 0.28 optics are the parallel-imaging setup.
Raster field is 15 by 15 micrometers with 1 micrometer steps and 15 micrometer hexagonal pitch; the separate high-resolution line step is 100 nm.
Analytical contact/reflectance model and finite-bit-depth estimate; the small-displacement example is a calculation.

evidence.locator: SI Note 2 pp. 5-7, Supplementary Table 1 and Fig. 2
evidence.fact: COMSOL explores probe, backing and sample deformation over hypothetical sample moduli; only stiff silicon imaging is experimentally demonstrated.
Cylinders on a compliant film are centered and indented by a calibrated conventional AFM; thermal PSD and rigid-glass optical sensitivity calibrate the lever.
A seven-probe simulation gives a 0.29 neighboring displacement fraction; this differs from the empirical 0.35 image correction.
Cylindrical-probe indentation is observed through sapphire with Nikon inverted brightfield, Grasshopper camera and 10x Olympus optics; the reported single-probe estimate is 6 nm.
Four identified probes provide within-probe and between-probe repeatability analysis; these are not four independent specimen replications.
Off-center normal indentation of a cylinder produces asymmetric optical deformation under torque; direct two-dimensional topographic-gradient mapping is prospective.

evidence.locator: Main Discussion and final Results paragraphs
evidence.fact: Large-array extension, MHz bandwidth, soft-sample capability and direct gradient mapping are prospective or calculated; flatness and vertical-range limitations remain.

evidence.locator: Main Data availability, Code availability, rights; SI p. 14 references
evidence.fact: Raw experiment data are available on request and external MATLAB code is linked; neither was inspected or executed in this conversion.
